passage.label: By fig olive; Mount Sinai; secure city Makkah; created man best stature; return him lowest low; Except believe righteous deeds reward uninterrupted

arabicExcerpts.text: لَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ فِيٓ أَحۡسَنِ تَقۡوِيمٖ
إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَٰتِ فَلَهُمۡ أَجۡرٌ غَيۡرُ مَمۡنُونٖ

mainSubject.label: Oaths by the fig, the olive, Mount Sinai and this secure city establishing that man was created in the best of stature then returned to the lowest of the low — except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for whom there is an uninterrupted reward

subordinateSubjects.label: Oath sworn by the fig and the olive
And by this secure city, Makkah
Man certainly created in the best of stature
Then returned to the lowest of the low
Except those who believe and do righteous deeds, receiving an uninterrupted reward

humanConditionsAndSpiritualStates.label: Man created in the best stature yet capable of descent to the lowest of the low
Belief joined to righteous deeds securing an uninterrupted reward as the exception

relationships.label: Four-fold oath by fig, olive, Sinai and secure city grounding the creation-descent narrative

notes: Wave 13 genuine re-extraction. Boundaries follow the text: P1 closes with the believing exception and its uninterrupted reward (6) before the rhetorical challenge opens (7); P2 covers the two-verse closing pair questioning denial and affirming divine justice (7-8).
